message.content:
**UNO – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | |------|--------------| | **1️⃣ Objective** | Be the first player to score at least 500 points across one or more rounds. Points come from opponents’ remaining cards when you finish a round. | | **2️⃣ Setup** | • Shuffle the standard UNO deck (108 cards).
• Deal each player seven face‑up cards.
• Place the top card of the draw pile face up; this starts the discard stack. If it’s an action card, follow its effect immediately before play begins. | | **3️⃣ Turn Order & Direction** | Players sit clockwise around the table. A “reverse” card flips direction instantly. | --- ### Card Types and Their Effects | Color | Number | Action | Wild Cards | |-------|--------|--------|------------| | Red/Green/Blue/Yellow | 0–9 | Play normally if matching color OR number. | *Wild* – choose new color. | | Same colors | Skip | Next player loses their turn. | *Wild Draw Four* – next player draws four AND chooses new color. Must only be played legally (no other playable card); otherwise penalty: draw six instead of four. | | Same colors | Reverse | Reverses play direction. | — | | Same colors | +2 / Draw Two | Next player draws two cards unless they counter with another +2 (stackable). | — | | Any color | Wild | Choose new color. | — | #### Stackability +2 and Wild Draw Four may be stacked: a player who receives them can reply with the same card type to pass the burden onto the next opponent. This continues until someone cannot respond, then that person takes all accumulated penalties. --- ### Playing Your Turn 1. **Match** either the color, number, symbol, or use a Wild/Wild Draw Four. - Example: Discard pile shows green 5 → You may play red 5, yellow 5, green 7, or any Wild. 2. **If no match**, you must draw one card from the stockpile. - If that drawn card matches, you may play it immediately on the same turn. - Otherwise your turn ends. 3. After playing, check whether you have zero cards left—if so, shout “UNO!” (or say “I’m out”) as soon as you’re down to one card. Failure to announce results in drawing two extra cards as a penalty. --- ### Ending a Round When a player discards their last card: 1. All other players tally the point values of their remaining hand: - Numbers: Face value (e.g., 8 = eight points) - Skip, Reverse, +2: 20 points each - Wild, Wild Draw Four: 50 points each 2. These totals add to the winner’s score. 3. Reset: reshuffle discarded cards into a fresh stockpile, deal again, and start a new round. A round can also end early if the stockpile runs out mid‑game; in that case, continue using the discard pile as a temporary stock until everyone has had equal turns, then restart the round. --- ### Winning the Game First player to reach ≥ 500 total points wins. Many casual groups shorten the target to 200 or even just keep playing single rounds without scoring. --- ### Common Variations (Optional) | Variation | How It Works | |-----------|-------------| | **“No Stacking”** | +2 and Wild Draw Four cannot be answered; the recipient simply draws the full amount. | | **“Stacked UNO”** | When a player goes out after stacking multiple +2s, the entire stack counts toward the winner’s score. | | **House Rules** | Some families allow “wild draw three,” “skip double,” or custom “action zones.” Always agree beforehand! | Enjoy mastering UNO’s fast pace and strategic depth!
